article.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
article.description: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.
article.content: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.

Ever said "I have visited Paris in 2019"? Here's the trick!

Use Present Perfect (have + past participle) for actions connected to now or when the exact time isn't stated, like "I have visited Paris." But for finished actions at a *specific* past time, always use Past Simple: "I visited Paris in 2019."

slides.body: The Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions connected to the present, or when the exact time isn't stated, like 'I have visited Paris.' In contrast, the Past Simple describes finished actions at a specific, stated past time, for example, 'I visited Paris in 2019.' A common mistake is using the Present Perfect with a specific past time marker. Therefore, 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect; you should use the Past Simple: 'I visited Paris in 2019.'
